what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat serious bacterial infections in the urinary tract and kidneys (called complicated urinary tract infections or cUTI). It works by killing bacteria that cause these infections, including some bacteria that are resistant to other antibiotics. It is given by a healthcare provider through an IV (intravenous) line directly into your vein, usually in a hospital or clinic setting.
how_to_take: This medicine is given to you by a nurse or doctor through an IV line in your vein. You will NOT give this medicine to yourself at home unless your doctor or care team has specifically trained you to do so. Each dose is given slowly over 3 hours. Do not skip any doses and try to finish the full course of treatment, even if you start to feel better early. Always let your nurse know if you feel any pain, burning, or notice swelling at the IV site during or after the infusion.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 4 grams (meropenem 2 g + vaborbactam 2 g) given every 8 hours (3 times a day) for 7 to 14 days. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have kidney problems. Always follow the dose and schedule your doctor has prescribed for you specifically.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given in a hospital or clinic by a healthcare provider, a missed dose is unlikely. However, if you are being treated at home and miss a dose, contact your home health nurse or doctor right away for guidance. Do not try to make up for a missed dose on your own or give yourself a double dose.
storage: This medicine is prepared and stored by pharmacy and healthcare professionals. If you are receiving it at home, store the prepared (mixed) medicine in the refrigerator (36°F to 46°F or 2°C to 8°C) for up to 12 hours, or at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 4 hours. Do not freeze it. Keep it out of reach of children. Do not use it if you notice particles, cloudiness, or discoloration in the bag or vial.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL medicines you take, including vitamins and supplements, before starting this medicine. Avoid taking valproic acid (used for seizures or mood disorders) while on this medicine, as meropenem-vaborbactam can lower valproic acid levels in your blood and may cause your seizures to return or worsen. Do not stop any medicine on your own without asking your doctor first. Avoid skipping doses or stopping treatment early, even if you feel better, as this can allow the infection to come back and make bacteria harder to treat.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help right away if you experience: a severe allergic reaction (hives, rash, swelling of your face, lips, tongue or throat, difficulty breathing, or dizziness); seizures or convulsions; severe diarrhea or diarrhea with blood or mucus, which could be a sign of a serious gut infection called C. difficile; severe skin reactions such as blistering or peeling skin; confusion, unusual behavior, or trouble thinking clearly; pain, redness, or swelling at your IV site; yellowing of skin or eyes; or any other new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting treatment, but it is very important to complete the full course of antibiotics as prescribed. Most people complete 7 to 14 days of treatment. Do not stop treatment early just because you feel better. Your doctor will monitor your progress with lab tests and check-ins to make sure the infection is clearing up properly.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your dose will likely be reduced if you have kidney disease or are on dialysis. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on how well your kidneys are working. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially kidney-related effects, and will be monitored closely. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of this medicine in pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established. Your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks with you. Children: Safety and dosing in children have not been fully established for this specific combination product.
